predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: the Badd highlands of Azerbaijan, "southward to near Ardabil and Marand, eastward to the Caspian Sea" and north to the Muqan steppe and the Aras bank

successors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
successors.text: Badd Fort and the highlands, taken by Afshin in 837

ledger.x: 819: the caliphate sends its first army.
837: the highlands return to the caliphate.
838: Babak is executed at Samira after Sahl ibn Sumbat hands him over: 'Babak's former ally Sahl ibn Sumbat handed him over' (14 March 838 on this page; probably 7 January 838 on the Babak page).

wars.name: Abbasid campaigns against Babak
wars.outcome: Yahya ibn Mu'adh (819-820), Isa ibn Muhammad (c.

wars.name: Khurramite rising around Hamadan
wars.outcome: After al-Ma'mun's death men from Jibal, Hamadan and Isfahan joined the movement and settled near Hamadan; the new army under Ishaq ibn Ibrahim defeated them (60,000 killed per al-Tabari).

certainty.note: A mountain redoubt: the extent comes from Arab historians' loose bounds (near Ardabil, Marand, the Aras, the Muqan steppe, the Caspian).
